india-macro.title: IFSCA working with govt on outbound tax issues: Official
india-macro.summary: Outbound investments from GIFT IFSC face tax-related constraints, according to an IFSCA official. The International Financial Services Centres Authority is actively collaborating with the government on this matter. Industry representatives have requested a more competitive tax framework to boost outbound investment structures.
india-macro.quick_take: The IFSCA is working with the government to address tax issues affecting outbound investments from GIFT IFSC, which could encourage more investment opportunities.
india-macro.simplified_article: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) reported that tax-related issues are hindering investments going out from GIFT IFSC. This collaboration with the government aims to create a better tax system for these investments. GIFT IFSC is a special financial zone in India meant to attract global finance. If tax obstacles are resolved, it could lead to more competitive investment structures, benefiting businesses and investors looking to expand internationally.
india-macro.investor_impact: If the tax framework improves, it could open doors for investors in sectors like finance and technology by making it cheaper and easier to invest abroad. india-macro.summary: Eight services sub-sectors recorded double-digit growth in May 2026. Accommodation and Food services saw a significant 27.4 percent increase. This growth was largely due to increased consumer activity in areas like accommodation and dining. However, some sectors like air transport and information broadcasting faced declines. This trend suggests a recovery in consumer spending in certain services, which might lead to more job opportunities. Businesses in sectors that grew are likely to benefit the most as demand continues to rise.

If you own investments in real estate, the positive growth there could also lead to increased property values.

This risk comes as generative AI continues to advance and integrate into various industries. Historically, technological advancements have caused disruptions in the job market, but they have also led to new growth opportunities. In the case of India, while some jobs will be lost, generative AI is expected to positively influence economic growth in the near future. india-macro.title: Import restriction on low-priced PVC resin may push domestic prices: GTRI
india-macro.summary: New import restrictions on low-priced PVC resin will affect foreign suppliers. Domestic prices for this key raw material are expected to increase significantly. India relies heavily on imports for its PVC resin needs. Domestic production capacity meets only a fraction of the country's demand. This measure will likely increase import costs without substantially reducing overall imports.
india-macro.quick_take: New import restrictions on low-priced PVC resin may raise domestic prices significantly, impacting industries that rely on this key raw material.
india-macro.simplified_article: India is imposing new import restrictions on low-priced PVC resin, a key material used in various products. This change will mainly affect foreign suppliers, causing domestic prices to rise because India mostly relies on imports for its PVC resin needs. Currently, local production can only meet a small part of the demand. As a result, companies that use PVC resin in their products will likely face higher costs, which might be passed on to consumers.
india-macro.investor_impact: Industries that use PVC resin, like construction and manufacturing, could see their production costs rise, which may lead to higher prices for consumers. If you're involved in these sectors, budget adjustments might be necessary as this could impact profit margins.

indian-markets.title: Amazon Web Services India net profit jumps over 10-fold to Rs 242 cr in FY26

crypto.title: Crypto Long & Short: What this year's $972 million crypto hacks actually tell us about security
crypto.summary: In this week's Crypto Long & Short, Immunefi's Mitchell Amador writes that most of 2026's stolen crypto is leaving through keys, signers and governance, not contract bugs, and explains why “we were audited” was never the same as “we are safe.”
crypto.quick_take: In 2026, $972 million worth of crypto was stolen, highlighting serious security flaws mostly due to poor key management, not software bugs.
crypto.simplified_article: This year, hackers stole $972 million in cryptocurrency, primarily due to weak management of security keys and governance rather than software errors. The issue arises because many crypto holders mistakenly believe that getting audits guarantees their safety. Audits ensure code is checked for safety, but they don’t protect against human errors in managing access keys. Moving forward, exchanges and crypto investors need to tighten security measures to prevent further hacks and protect their assets.
crypto.investor_impact: If you hold cryptocurrency, this news indicates that you should be more cautious about how your keys and access are managed. Poor key security can lead to significant losses, similar to the recent $972 million worth of hacks, impacting many investors. This could lead to increased insurance costs or stricter security requirements for crypto services, which might affect fees and accessibility.

key_terms.meaning: Keys are digital credentials that allow you to access and control your cryptocurrency, and poor management can lead to theft.
